oven-convection-fan.context: A square oven frame with a three-bladed fan in the middle. It marks the fan oven or convection setting on oven dials, control panels and cooking charts.

oven-top-heat.context: A square oven frame with a bar along the top and a baking dish below it. It stands for the top heat setting used to brown the surface of a dish.

oven-bottom-heat.context: A square oven frame with a bar along the bottom and a baking dish above it. It stands for the bottom heat setting used for crisp bases, pizza and pies.

oven-top-bottom-heat.context: A square oven frame with a bar at the top, a bar at the bottom and a baking dish between them. It shows the conventional or static oven setting with top and bottom elements.

oven-grill-element.context: A square oven frame with a zigzag heating element along the top. It is the grill or broil setting found on oven dials and cooker manuals.

oven-light.context: A square oven frame with a light bulb in the center. It marks the control that switches on the oven lamp so you can check food without opening the door.

oven-fan-grill.context: A square oven frame with a zigzag grill element on top and a small fan below it. It marks the fan grill setting, which blows hot air while the top element is on.

oven-ring-heat.context: A square oven frame holding a small fan inside a round ring element. It stands for the fan forced or true convection setting where a ring heater and fan work together.

oven-fan-bottom-heat.context: A square oven frame with a small fan above a bar along the bottom. It marks the pizza or convection bake setting with bottom heat and circulating air.

oven-defrost.context: A square oven frame with a small fan next to a water drop. It is the defrost or thaw setting that circulates air without strong heat.

oven-steam-mode.context: A square oven frame with three wavy lines rising inside it. It stands for the steam cooking setting on combi and steam ovens.

dish-towel.context: A rectangular towel hanging from a loop at the top, with two stripes across the lower part and a wavy hem. Use it for drying dishes, kitchen linen and tea towel shopping.

keep-warm.context: A plate covered by a dome with three wavy heat lines rising above it. It marks a keep warm function on ovens, slow cookers and food warmers, and warm serving in general.

dishwasher-safe.context: A plate and a glass standing in a rack with water drops falling on them. It is the care label for items that can go in the dishwasher.

oven-safe.context: A covered dish inside an oven outline with a small flame underneath. It is the label for cookware and bakeware that can go in a hot oven.

freezer-safe.context: A snowflake above a small lidded food container. It is the label for containers and bags that can be used in the freezer.

food-safe-symbol.context: A wine glass beside a fork, the common mark for materials that are safe to touch food and drink. It appears on cups, plates, containers and packaging.

induction-compatible.context: A pot above a horizontal line with a looped coil underneath. It is the label for pans that work on induction hobs and for induction cooktops.

colander.context: A deep perforated bowl with handles on the rim and a ring foot. Use it for draining pasta, rinsing vegetables and straining boiled food.

mesh-strainer.context: A round fine mesh basket with a long handle and a hook on the rim that rests on a bowl. Use it for sifting flour, straining tea and rinsing small grains.

service-bell.context: A dome counter bell with a push button on top and a flat base, with small lines showing it ringing. It is used for front desks, reception counters and calling for service.

dough-whisk.context: A wooden handle with a pointed wire loop crossed by two wires, turned on a diagonal. It is used for stirring heavy bread dough and batter without sticking.

cake-leveler.context: A U-shaped wire frame standing on two feet with a thin cutting wire stretched across, slicing through a cake. Bakers use it to cut even layers and level the top.

herb-scissors.context: Scissors with a comb of parallel blades on two crossing ring handles. They snip herbs such as chives and parsley into fine even pieces.

rotary-grater.context: A drum grater with a hand crank on one side and a grip handle below it. It is used to grate hard cheese, nuts and chocolate at the table or in the kitchen.

campfire-pot.context: A cooking pot hanging under a tripod of poles with small flames below. It stands for camp cooking over an open fire and outdoor stews.

vertical-rotisserie.context: A tall cone of stacked meat on an upright spit with a heating panel beside it. It represents doner kebab, shawarma, gyros and al pastor shops.

cereal-dispenser.context: A tall hopper filled with cereal pieces with a tapered spout above a bowl. It stands for breakfast cereal dispensers, dry food storage and self serve breakfast bars.

napkin-holder.context: A low open holder with a fan of paper napkins standing in it. Use it for table settings, diners and picnic or dining supplies.

rinsing-produce.context: A tap with a water drop falling onto two vegetables sitting in a colander. It illustrates washing fruit and vegetables before cooking or eating.

washing-dishes.context: Plates standing in a sink basin with soap bubbles floating above. It stands for washing up, dishwashing chores and kitchen cleaning.

chef-jacket.context: A double-breasted white jacket with a stand collar and two rows of round buttons. It is the uniform of professional cooks and stands for restaurant kitchens and culinary staff.

order-ticket-rail.context: A horizontal rail with three paper order tickets hanging from it, each with a notched bottom. Restaurant kitchens use it to line up dockets for the cooks.

recipe-box.context: An open box of index cards with a raised divider tab standing above the rest. Cooks keep handwritten and saved recipes in it.

knife-sharpener.context: A block with a V-shaped slot and a kitchen knife lowered into it, blade pointing down. It stands for pull-through knife sharpeners and keeping blades sharp.

knife-roll.context: An unrolled fabric wrap with a row of pockets holding knife handles and a tie strap at the side. Chefs carry their knives in it to work and culinary school.

rising-dough.context: A bowl covered with a cloth that a dome of dough pushes up from underneath. It shows proofing bread dough and yeast baking.

meat-claws.context: A pair of shredding claws, each with a grip handle and a row of long pointed tines. They pull apart cooked pork, chicken and brisket.

chestnut-pan.context: A shallow perforated pan with a long handle holding roasting chestnuts, with a few shown on top. It is used over an open fire or a stove in autumn and winter.

soft-serve-machine.context: A box machine with a lever sitting above a swirled ice cream cone. It stands for soft serve stands, frozen yogurt shops and ice cream machines.

plate-stack.context: Three dinner plates stacked on top of each other, seen from the side. Use it for dishes, tableware and dinnerware.

grill-press.context: A flat iron weight with ridges underneath and a handle on top. It presses bacon, burgers and sandwiches flat on a grill or griddle.

lemon-squeezer.context: A cup holding a lemon half with a pair of long hinged handles. It stands for hand citrus presses used to juice lemons and limes.

vegetable-dicer.context: A box with small diced cubes inside and a lifted lid whose underside is a grid of blades. It stands for chopper boxes that cut onions and vegetables into even pieces.

pulling-noodles.context: Two fists stretching long noodle strands that hang in loops between them. It shows hand pulled noodle making, as in la mian shops.

sizzling-platter.context: A cast iron serving plate on a wooden board with three wavy steam lines rising from it. Restaurants use it for fajitas and steaks served hot at the table.

kitchen-counter.context: A wall cabinet above a worktop with a tap, over a base cabinet with two doors and knobs. It stands for kitchen design, fitted units and kitchen remodeling.

cornbread-pan.context: A cast iron tray with a row of corn-cob shaped wells seen from above. It bakes corn sticks and stands for southern cornbread.

korean-bbq-grill.context: A domed ribbed grill plate with a drain rim sitting over a small gas flame. It shows tabletop Korean barbecue where guests grill pork belly and beef themselves.

ladling-soup.context: A ladle tilted over a bowl with a stream of soup pouring from its lip. It is used for serving soup, stew and broth, and for soup kitchens.

bottle-carrier.context: An open crate holding four bottles with a handle rising from the center divider. It stands for carrying beer, soda and wine bottles home or to a picnic.

taco-holder.context: A low stand holding two tacos upright, with frilly filling over the top of each shell. Use it for taco night, Mexican restaurants and taco serving.

sticky-rice-steamer.context: A tall woven cone basket sitting in the mouth of a pot with steam rising above it. It is the traditional way to steam sticky rice in Thai and Lao cooking.

chimney-starter.context: An upright steel cylinder with a side handle and flames rising from its top. Grill cooks use it to light charcoal without lighter fluid.

stove-lighter.context: A long thin wand with a trigger grip and a small flame at its tip. It lights gas stoves, grills, candles and fireplaces from a safe distance.

cookbook-stand.context: An open book with lines of text resting upright in a trough-shaped stand. It keeps a recipe book propped up and clean on the kitchen counter.

squeezing-lemon.context: A fist pressing a lemon half with juice drops falling from it. It shows juicing by hand and adding lemon juice to recipes and drinks.

utensil-rail.context: A wall rail with a ladle, a spatula and a whisk hanging from it. It stands for hanging kitchen utensils within easy reach.

mesh-food-cover.context: A collapsible mesh dome with ribs and a small knob, standing over a plate. It keeps flies off food at picnics, barbecues and outdoor meals.

fish-scaler.context: A short handle with a toothed head and small scales flying off to the side. It removes scales from a whole fish before cooking.

spaghetti-measure.context: A flat disc with a handle and round holes that grow larger along a diagonal. Cooks push dry spaghetti through the holes to measure one, two or more portions.

ice-sphere-mold.context: A round two-part mold with a seam around its middle and a small fill hole on top. It makes large clear ice balls for whiskey and cocktails.

citrus-zester.context: A long flat grater blade with rows of tiny holes on a short handle, with thin zest curls beside it. It takes fine zest from lemons, limes and oranges.

pineapple-corer.context: A tall tube with a spiral blade and a bar handle on top, pushed through a pineapple ring. It cuts out the core and slices the fruit in one twist.

molinillo.context: A carved wooden stick with a bulbous ringed head and loose rings around it, turned on a diagonal. It is rolled between the palms to froth Mexican hot chocolate.

mooncake-mold.context: A plunger press with a top handle pushing down on a patterned round cake below it. It stands for mooncake baking during the Mid-Autumn Festival.

spit-roast.context: A joint of meat on a horizontal spit resting between two posts over flames, with a crank at one end. It shows hog roasts, campfire roasting and outdoor rotisserie cooking.

noodle-basket.context: A deep cylindrical wire basket with a long straight handle, turned on a diagonal. Cooks lower it into boiling water to cook and lift out noodles or fry food.

salt-block.context: A rectangular salt slab with crystal facets and a thin slice of meat cooking on top, with steam above. It stands for searing and serving on Himalayan salt blocks.

grilling-plank.context: A rectangular wooden plank with grain lines and a fish fillet lying on it. It is used to grill or smoke salmon and other fish on the barbecue.

metate.context: A sloped grinding stone on short legs with a cylindrical hand stone resting across it. It is the traditional Mesoamerican tool for grinding corn, cacao and chiles.

roti-rolling-board.context: A round raised board on short feet with a tapered rolling pin lying across it. South Asian kitchens use it to roll out roti, chapati and paratha.

rice-ball-mold.context: A triangular mold with a press lid on a stem handle. It shapes rice into onigiri triangles for bento boxes and snacks.

sushi-rice-tub.context: A wide shallow wooden tub with two metal bands and a flat paddle resting on its rim. Sushi chefs cool and season rice in it.

bamboo-wok-brush.context: A bundle of thin bamboo strips tied with a band near the top and fanning out at the bottom. It scrubs woks and pans clean without harsh chemicals.

coconut-scraper.context: A low stool with a serrated round blade sticking out from one end. The cook sits on it and scrapes a coconut half against the blade to shred the flesh.

spaetzle-maker.context: A flat perforated plate with a handle and a box hopper that slides along it. Cooks press soft batter through the holes into boiling water to make spaetzle noodles.
